name: Quarterly Business Review
description: For leadership operating reviews: enterprise-blue structure, disciplined RAG status coding, owner-based scorecards, quantified wins, explicit risks, and due-dated next-quarter actions.
style_guide:
# Quarterly Business Review

## Design intent

Create a leadership-ready quarterly business review that turns one operating period into a compact chain of accountability: objectives, performance, wins, gaps, forward risks, and next-quarter actions. The design is clean, rigorous, and pre-read friendly: enterprise blue for structure, exact green/amber/red status semantics, white analytical pages, square cards, large tables, small monospaced metadata, named owners, and explicit dates. It should feel like a controlled operating document rather than a celebratory report or dashboard collage.

Every page must state one conclusion and make the evidence, owner, variance, and decision visible. Preserve the visual grammar shown by the previews, but never copy their company, people, metrics, customers, suppliers, dates, targets, risks, or action items. Preview images are UI-only references; this written guide is the complete authoring authority.

## Core visual signature

- Use Enterprise blue as the structural color for the cover, score bands, table headers, priority cards, section labels, chart series, and navigation.
- Reserve Green, Amber, and Red strictly for operational status. Define the thresholds and apply them consistently across objectives, KPI cards, risks, due dates, and charts.
- Pair bold sans-serif conclusion headlines with a neutral sans-serif evidence layer and tracked monospaced metadata.
- Use square, flat, border-led components. Avoid shadows, rounded dashboard cards, decorative icons, and ornamental graphics.
- Show named owners beside objectives, KPIs, wins, risks, priorities, and actions. A status without an accountable owner is incomplete.
- Keep one idea per slide and three to five evidence points or structures. Dense content must remain inspectable as a leadership pre-read.

## Canvas, grid, and spacing

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px` canvas in a 16:9 ratio.
- Keep `48 px` left and right safe margins and `28–36 px` top and bottom safe margins. No source, status, owner, or due date may touch the edge.
- Use a 12-column grid with `14–18 px` gutters. Align title edges, card boundaries, table columns, chart axes, risk grids, and footer marks to shared columns.
- Reserve `78–106 px` for the metadata, title, and subtitle region on body pages. Leave `24–34 px` before the main exhibit.
- Use `16–22 px` between major panels and `10–14 px` between labels, values, and supporting evidence.
- Keep a quiet footer band of `22–30 px` for sources, threshold definitions, cadence notes, and `PAGE NN / NN`.
- The cover is a deliberate split composition: roughly `43/57`, with an Enterprise-blue title field on the left and a white meeting-brief field on the right, separated by a thin Red seam.
- Prefer aligned rows and columns over floating modules. Reading order should remain obvious from upper-left to lower-right.

## Color system

### Foundation colors

- Enterprise blue: `#005EB8`. Use for the cover field, objective summary band, primary chart series, table headers, priority cards, section codes, active timeline markers, and structural rules.
- Stage white: `#FFFFFF`. Use as the dominant body-page canvas and the primary reverse text on Enterprise blue.
- Cool panel: `#F4F6F9`. Use for meeting agendas, neutral table headers, risk probability cells, and secondary evidence groups.
- Alternating row: `#FAFBFC`. Use for table striping and subtle separation between dense evidence rows.
- Primary ink: `#1B1B1B`. Use for titles, decisive values, table labels, and critical explanatory copy.
- Body slate: `#5A6271`. Use for subtitles, supporting copy, chart labels, owner roles, and source notes.
- Structural line: `#DDE1E6`. Use for one-pixel borders, table rules, axes, and card dividers.
- Quiet blue: `#669FD5`. Use for secondary blue values, inactive milestone states, and low-emphasis information on Enterprise blue.

### RAG status colors

- On-plan green: `#3E8E4F`. Use only for met or exceeded targets, completed actions, verified positive outcomes, and controlled risk.
- Watch amber: `#D9A700`. Use for within-threshold misses, emerging risk, partial completion, or a condition requiring management attention.
- Miss red: `#A6192E`. Use for material target misses, overdue decisions, high-severity risk, failed control, or a gap requiring intervention.
- White: `#FFFFFF`. Use for labels on solid Green, Amber when contrast permits, Red, and Enterprise blue. Use Primary ink on Amber when white contrast is insufficient.

### Color discipline

- Enterprise blue carries structure, never performance status. RAG colors carry status, never decoration or department identity.
- Publish the actual RAG thresholds in the footer or source note. The same metric must not change color because of narrative preference.
- Keep saturated RAG fills small: top rails, compact badges, selected values, probability/impact cells, or one risk card edge.
- Use no more than one RAG status per KPI or risk unless showing a clearly labeled state transition.
- Never rely on color alone. Pair every status with `GREEN`, `YELLOW` or `AMBER`, `RED`, a score, variance, due-date state, or other direct text.
- Use flat fills only. Do not add gradients, glow, glass effects, or colored shadows.

## Typography

- Primary font: `Inter`, with `Arial`, `Helvetica Neue`, or a comparable system sans-serif as fallback.
- Metadata font: `IBM Plex Mono`, with `Consolas` or `Courier New` as fallback. Use it for slide codes, periods, section labels, sources, units, status badges, thresholds, and dates.
- For CJK output, use a common CJK sans-serif with strong bold weights and a CJK-capable monospaced face only for short metadata. Preserve hierarchy without forcing wide Latin tracking.
- Cover title: `48–58 px`, weight `800–900`, line-height `1.02–1.08`, Stage white. Use three short lines when needed.
- Body-page title: `32–40 px`, weight `700–800`, line-height `1.06–1.14`, Primary ink. Write it as the operating conclusion or page purpose.
- Subtitle: `14–17 px`, weight `400–500`, line-height `1.4–1.5`, Body slate.
- Hero metric: `38–52 px`, weight `700–800`, using tabular numerals.
- Card title: `18–22 px`, weight `700–800`; table and body copy: `11–14 px`, weight `400–600`, line-height `1.35–1.5`.
- Metadata, status labels, chart units, footer rules, periods, and sources: `8–10 px`, metadata face, weight `500–700`, uppercase when appropriate, letter-spacing `1.2–2.2 px`.
- Do not shrink table text to preserve every row. Summarize, group, or move operational detail to an appendix.

## Page frame and navigation

- Begin body pages with a small blue monospaced line at upper-left containing slide number and page role. Place period, scoring rule, or display convention at upper-right.
- Use a strong, left-aligned title and a one-sentence subtitle that summarizes the evidence and decision context.
- The footer contains source or control information at left and the page number at right. Include data-lock time, reporting window, and threshold definition where relevant.
- On the cover, the left field contains the QBR identity, period, document classification, main title, operating promise, and narrative sequence.
- The right cover field contains review date, presenter and business-unit metadata, the six-page agenda, next-review date, and page count.
- Do not use a generic agenda slide after the cover when the meeting brief already provides the sequence.

## Cards, scorebands, and tables

- Use square corners: `0–2 px` radius. Cards have `1 px` Structural line borders and no shadow.
- A thin `5–7 px` top rail may express the card's RAG state. Do not fill the entire card unless it is a summary band, priority, or risk impact cell.
- Objective summary bands use Enterprise blue with three large metrics and a compact status-spread group.
- KPI cards follow a fixed hierarchy: lens and status, KPI title, hero value, plan variance, six-period trend, supporting metrics, and named owner.
- Win cards state the outcome, the mechanism that produced it, quantified evidence, repeatability, owner, and what priority it feeds. Avoid calling normal delivery a win without comparison or causal evidence.
- Gap cards state the missed result, the causal mechanism, quantified effect, owner, mitigation, and timing.
- Risk cards state risk category, event, time horizon, evidence, probability, impact, mitigation owner, and decide-by date.
- Action tables use a blue header, alternating white rows, compact descriptions, a definition of done, a single named owner, and a due date.
- Keep statuses rectangular and compact. Do not use decorative pills or ambiguous traffic-light dots.

## Charts and scorecards

- Prefer six-period bar or line trends, compact plan-versus-actual values, objective score tables, risk probability-impact cells, and milestone timelines.
- Use Enterprise blue for the primary trend. Use Green, Amber, or Red only for the latest state, threshold line, or directly related variance.
- Chart grids and axes use Structural line. Remove legends when series can be directly labeled.
- Show the target or threshold as a labeled dashed line where relevant. Do not use a cropped axis to exaggerate variance.
- Every KPI must include unit, reporting period, source, actual, target or comparator, and RAG rule.
- Objective scoring must state the scale, aggregation method, target score, and meaning of each status band.
- Probability and impact should be based on an explicit assessment window and materiality definition. Do not show pseudo-precise percentages without an agreed method.
- Directly label the latest value and material variance. Keep historical values small but readable.

## Adaptable composition families

These are composition tendencies, not executable templates, a mandatory sequence, or permission to reuse preview content. Choose the structure that best supports the actual review.

- Cover and meeting brief: use the blue/white split cover with the reporting period, confidentiality, presenter metadata, compact agenda, and next-review date.
- Objectives and key results: use a full-width blue score band above an owner-based table of three to five objectives with target, actual, normalized score, and explicit status.
- Performance scorecard: use three equal columns for the most important operating lenses. Each column contains one hero KPI, one short trend, three or four supporting metrics, and an owner.
- Wins and drivers: use a `2 × 2` grid of quantified win cards. Every card names the mechanism, repeatability, owner, and next-quarter implication.
- Gaps and risks: place three current gaps above three forward risks. Use Red for material misses and High risk, Amber for medium watch items, and explicit probability, impact, mitigation, and decision dates.
- Next-quarter priorities and actions: use three Enterprise-blue priority cards above an action table and a due-date timeline. Every action must have one definition of done, owner, and date.
- Financial review alternative: use a score band for revenue, margin, cash, and forecast accuracy, then a bridge or variance table with an owner and corrective action for each material deviation.
- Customer review alternative: use renewal, expansion, service, and adoption lenses with cohort-consistent trends, named account actions, and a short escalation register.
- Operations review alternative: use safety, quality, delivery, cost, and capacity metrics, followed by a root-cause exhibit and an owner-based recovery plan.

## Content truth and reporting controls

- Treat every preview organization, person, metric, customer, supplier, target, date, score, risk, and action as fictional reference content. Never reuse it unless independently grounded in the current Workspace.
- Never invent revenue, ARR, margin, cash flow, pipeline, churn, retention, NPS, CSAT, delivery, quality, yield, hiring, attrition, safety, cost, or forecast figures.
- Distinguish actual, preliminary, estimate, forecast, plan, budget, target, stretch, prior-period, and year-over-year comparisons. Do not mix bases inside one scorecard.
- State whether a quarter is fiscal or calendar, the exact reporting dates, currency, consolidation scope, and data-lock timestamp.
- Do not label a metric Green merely because it improved. Green means it met the published plan or threshold.
- Separate correlation from mechanism. A win driver or gap cause must be supported by evidence; otherwise label it as a hypothesis requiring validation.
- Risks must have an assessment horizon, probability basis, impact basis, mitigation, owner, and decision or review date. Do not invent precision to fill a risk card.
- Each action needs one accountable owner, due date, definition of done, dependency where material, and review cadence. Avoid shared ownership without a single directly responsible person.
- Customer, employee, supplier, or partner names require accurate status and appropriate permission. Do not disclose sensitive information beyond the intended review audience.
- If evidence is incomplete, mark the metric preliminary, show the data gap, use a clearly labeled `TBD`, or omit the claim. Never fill a scorecard with plausible values.

## Allowed variation

- Preserve the white canvas, Enterprise-blue structure, exact RAG semantics, bold sans-serif titles, monospaced metadata, square components, owner discipline, and due-date visibility.
- The deck may cover a company, business unit, function, product line, geography, or program. Adapt the lenses and terminology without changing the accountability grammar.
- Use two to four lenses instead of three when the operating model requires it. Give each lens enough width for legible evidence.
- A section may use a full-width blue band or cards, but ordinary body pages should remain predominantly white.
- Adapt capitalization, tracking, line breaks, number formats, date formats, and status words to the confirmed output language while keeping thresholds explicit.

## Avoid

- Do not reproduce preview facts, people, targets, risks, actions, or customer and supplier names. Transfer the operating-review grammar only.
- Do not use gradients, lifestyle photography, decorative illustrations, 3D charts, glass effects, glowing metrics, rounded SaaS cards, or dashboard icon grids.
- Do not use Green, Amber, or Red as department colors or aesthetic accents. They are reserved for status.
- Do not celebrate wins without stating the causal mechanism, repeatability, and next action.
- Do not list risks without probability, impact, mitigation owner, and a decision or review date.
- Do not use broad priorities without executable actions, definitions of done, owners, and due dates.
- Do not show more than five top-level objectives, four ordinary KPI lenses, four wins, or three top risks on one main page. Move detail to backup pages.
- Do not shrink sources, chart labels, owner names, or due dates below readable size.
- Do not hide unfavorable results, change thresholds retrospectively, combine unlike periods, or omit the data-lock date.
